result:
The DEC-468 cases are written and committed as `e0b438501e856ee65078fe4c8eaa9af1bd7ed8ce` on `w1/W1-38`.

## New cases (8)

| Case | Compares | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `TestOpenSpecSkills::test_generated_skill_is_the_one_openspec_ships[<skill>]` × 6 | Every file `openspec init --tools claude` (1.13.2) writes under `.claude/skills/<skill>/` with the generated file of that name. `SKILL.md` is compared by body byte for byte and by frontmatter as a mapping. | **6 red**: none of the six `SKILL.md` is generated, because no registered source exists. |
| `TestOpenSpecSkills::test_no_openspec_skill_that_openspec_does_not_ship` | The `openspec-*` folder names under `.claude/skills/` against the names OpenSpec ships. | **Green** today, since no `openspec-*` skill is generated at all; it stays as the guard against one written for the ticket. |
| `TestDeleteProtection::test_delete_preserves_openspec_skills` | After `generate --delete`, all six skills are still there as OpenSpec ships them (same comparison). | **Red**: all six report `SKILL.md: not there`. |

The six skills are `openspec-apply-change`, `openspec-archive-change`, `openspec-explore`, `openspec-propose`, `openspec-sync-specs` and `openspec-update-change`, one `SKILL.md` each.

The comparison is reachable: in a temporary folder, `rulesync import` followed by `rulesync generate --delete` (24.0.0) gave each of the six back with the same body and the same frontmatter values.

## Counts

- **Suite:** 67 cases in 17 classes — 40 green, 27 red, 0 skipped (full run to its end, 58.8 s).
- **Before this round:** 59 cases — 39 green, 20 red.
- **Added:** 8 cases — 7 red, 1 green. The totals move by exactly the eight new cases.

## Beyond the new cases

- **Fixture split:** the OpenSpec fixture is now one `openspec init` run that both the command cases and the skill cases read. The seven existing OpenSpec cases are unchanged in what they assert.
- **README:** it now states the skill tolerance (the same one as the other skills, plus frontmatter as a mapping, as for the commands), DEC-469 in one line, and P-1 and P-2 as decided.

## For the orchestrator

The guard hook refused two of my Bash commands — one writing under a variable path, one using a heredoc — so I made the edits with the Edit tool instead. The decision register was only read from the main tree, and no writing rulesync command ran in the worktree.
